page.layout: One page of text, one printed page on the scan. Top: running head "VARIA POEMATA." with page number "IOI" at the right. Then the end of a poem (verse fragment), the author's initials "I. I. B." at the right, a rule, the title "IOANNI DVRANTIO.", and the poem in full. Signature "G. ij." at the foot. No margin notes.

p.i: Et doctum fidibus dicere Gallicis: Quæ non livor edax nec mora temporum Saturnúsve truci falce potens metet.

HEu, Chiragra, malum ferox, furensque Furui filia Tartari, miserellos Quæ diris, Stygijs, feris, tremendis Mortales cruciatibus fatigas, Nostro parce, precor, precor Duranto: Parce, nec manibus nocere fas sit Centum, quas colit, artium peritis, Et centum simul elegantiarum. Hoc rogant Charites, novémque Musæ, Et Phœbus citharæ parens canoræ, Et quæ concutit Ægidem Minerua: Omnes illius hoc rogant amici. Olim non habuit sagaciores Manus Cecropius faber, biformi Qui monstro posuit vagas latebras, Errantésque vias domus nefandæ: Qui primas docuit volare ceras. Sphæra non habuit senex repertor Manus Archimedes peritiores,

page.notes: The page's first verse line and the "miserellos" line end the page's poem fragment; the poem's line-ends are kept as printed. The "IOI" page number and the signature "G. ij." are read as printed. Doubtful: "HEu" with the initial H as a large initial is transcribed as printed. "Furui" and "precor Duranto" are as printed, with no emendation.
